concerns.text: FR-001 mandates human‑annotated feasibility scores for *all* 1 000 prompts, but the original idea only requires enough human scores to evaluate the baseline vs. graph‑augmented conditions. Requiring the full 1 000 annotations adds unnecessary scope and conflicts with FR‑009 (which only requires 200).

FR-007 requires a multiple‑comparison correction (Bonferroni or Benjamini‑Hochberg). The idea describes a single paired test; adding this correction expands the scope beyond what is needed to answer the research question.

FR-008 imposes a 6‑hour runtime and ≤ 7 GB RAM budget. These performance constraints were not part of the original idea and constitute an extra engineering requirement not required to test the hypothesis.

The spec cites three InstructPix2Pix parquet shards as the raw prompt source, yet InstructPix2Pix contains only single‑step edits and no naturally occurring conflicting instructions. This dataset cannot validly test the core hypothesis about multi‑step/conflicting prompts, causing a methodological mismatch with the idea.

The spec adds quantitative thresholds (e.g., correlation ≥ 0.5, effect size ≥ 0.5) that were not present in the idea. Introducing these thresholds redefines the research question into “does the system achieve these preset metrics,” which drifts from the original question of whether symbolic graphs mitigate degradation.

FR-009 specifies collecting human feasibility scores for at least 200 prompts, yet the plan (and FR‑001) assumes scores for the full 1 000 prompts for paired analysis. This inconsistency creates an under‑specified data collection scope and may leave the study under‑powered.
